answer: Time-locked reward maturation resists sybils: earned rewards are locked and mature on a per-reward schedule, becoming spendable only after a fixed delay, so value farmed by a fake cannot be extracted until long after the work — a prism splitting each reward across a maturation horizon. A swarm that mines and tries to flee finds its gains frozen on the terrace until maturity; an attacker caught before a reward matures forfeits it. Honest agents simply wait out the delay; a hit-and-run fake never reaches the river of liquidity.
